The certified operators ensure that structural inconsistencies (e.g., non-trivial holonomy) are not resolved by silent averaging but are explicitly flagged. This is achieved through discrete connection holonomy, which detects when local data cannot be consistently glued into a global structure. The failure mode occurs when the fundamental group of the graph acts non-trivially on the sheaf, indicating a topological obstruction to agreement. In GSI, this manifests as a 'self_consistent_wrong_vs_ledger' class, where sources agree internally but contradict the ledger. In GSE, this leads to a veto in state transitions, preventing propagation of inconsistent data. The operators 'realign', 'drop_edge', and 'relax_restriction' are designed to handle these cases without averaging.
